searches.outcome: The official publisher landing and PDF URLs were recorded as cookie-wall failures; the Vista full-book mirror was recorded with its TLS verification failure. Searched for complete independent lecture-note sources and verified the full NYU 24-page Learning signal representations lecture notes (PDF pp. 8-12 contain PCA definitions, projection variance, sample covariance, and finite-moment Chebyshev consistency) plus the complete Mukherjee Lecture 8 note. All mathematical claims are locally proved or supported by these accessible treatments; no coverage is waived.

alternatives.argument: The full definition is carried locally: covariance-PCA orders the kernels of the covariance matrix; correlation-PCA applies D^{-1} to centered coordinates only when each variance is positive; the sample convention uses the n-divisor sample-centered covariance. The covariance target is well-defined by the finite-second-moment covariance result. The sample map measurability result lem-pca-sample-covariance-is-a-measurable-estimator is declared in justified_by and proves this well-definedness obligation.

For any unit a, finite-sum expectation expansion gives Var(a^T X)=a^T Sigma a. In an orthonormal eigenbasis, this equals sum_j lambda_j c_j^2<=lambda_1; equality occurs exactly in the top eigenspace. The same calculation applies after positive-standard-deviation standardization.

The spectral theorem gives an orthonormal eigenbasis. If lambda_1=lambda_2, the kernel ker(Sigma-lambda_1 I) contains two linearly independent eigenvectors. Every unit vector in that kernel maximizes the Rayleigh quotient, so the whole kernel is canonical and no one vector is selected.

For each entry, the oracle-centered product average has variance at most E[Y_j^2 Y_k^2]/n; summing gives an O(1/n) Frobenius second moment. The sample-centered matrix subtracts bar(Y)bar(Y)^T, whose Frobenius norm is ||bar(Y)||^2 and whose root-n-scaled Markov tail tends to zero. The triangle inequality gives the claimed root-n bound.

Courant-Fischer bounds lambda_1(A+E) between lambda_1(A)-epsilon and lambda_1(A)+epsilon, and bounds lambda_2(A+E) by lambda_2(A)+epsilon using v-perp. Projecting the perturbed eigen-equation onto v-perp and inverting lambda_tilde_1 I-A on that subspace gives ||P_vperp v_tilde||<=epsilon/(g-epsilon).

Each coordinate of the displayed sample-centered covariance is a polynomial in the finite sample coordinates, hence the matrix map is continuous and Borel. Its target is the covariance estimand, so the statistic and estimator definitions apply.

The sample covariance root-n Frobenius bound implies an operator-norm root-n bound. On epsilon_n<g/2 the local perturbation theorem gives angle<=2 epsilon_n/g and a unique sample top line; this event has probability tending to one. Boundedness in probability at root-n scale yields convergence of the sign-free angle to zero.
For I_2 the top kernel is R^2, so every unit line is leading. For diag(2,1) the top kernel is span(e_1), but e_1 and -e_1 are both unit eigenvectors on that line.

On the explicit four-point law, E(U)=E(V)=E(UV)=0 and E(U^2)=E(V^2)=1. This gives Sigma=[[9,3],[3,4]], D=diag(3,2), and R=[[1,1/2],[1/2,1]]. R has top line span(1,1); Sigma has distinct eigenvalues (13±sqrt(61))/2 and maps (1,1) to (12,7), so its leading line differs.

A_delta=diag(1+delta,1) has gap delta and E_delta=[[0,delta/4],[delta/4,0]] has norm delta/4. The perturbed top eigenvalue is 1+delta/2+sqrt(5)delta/4 and its eigenvector slope is sqrt(5)-2, so the angle is fixed while delta tends to zero.

All mathematical claims are locally proved or supported by these accessible treatments; no coverage is waived.

alternatives.argument: The full definition is carried locally: covariance-PCA orders the kernels of the covariance matrix; correlation-PCA applies D^{-1} to centered coordinates only when each variance is positive; the sample convention uses the n-divisor sample-centered covariance. The covariance target is well-defined by the finite-second-moment covariance result. The sample map measurability result lem-pca-sample-covariance-is-a-measurable-estimator is declared in justified_by and proves this well-definedness obligation.

For any unit a, finite-sum expectation expansion gives Var(a^T X)=a^T Sigma a. In an orthonormal eigenbasis, this equals sum_j lambda_j c_j^2<=lambda_1; equality occurs exactly in the top eigenspace. The same calculation applies after positive-standard-deviation standardization.

The spectral theorem gives an orthonormal eigenbasis. If lambda_1=lambda_2, the kernel ker(Sigma-lambda_1 I) contains two linearly independent eigenvectors. Every unit vector in that kernel maximizes the Rayleigh quotient, so the whole kernel is canonical and no one vector is selected.

For each entry, the oracle-centered product average has variance at most E[Y_j^2 Y_k^2]/n; summing gives an O(1/n) Frobenius second moment. The sample-centered matrix subtracts bar(Y)bar(Y)^T, whose Frobenius norm is ||bar(Y)||^2 and whose root-n-scaled Markov tail tends to zero. The triangle inequality gives the claimed root-n bound.

Courant-Fischer bounds lambda_1(A+E) between lambda_1(A)-epsilon and lambda_1(A)+epsilon, and bounds lambda_2(A+E) by lambda_2(A)+epsilon using v-perp. Projecting the perturbed eigen-equation onto v-perp and inverting lambda_tilde_1 I-A on that subspace gives ||P_vperp v_tilde||<=epsilon/(g-epsilon).

Each coordinate of the displayed sample-centered covariance is a polynomial in the finite sample coordinates, hence the matrix map is continuous and Borel. Its target is the covariance estimand, so the statistic and estimator definitions apply.

The sample covariance root-n Frobenius bound implies an operator-norm root-n bound. On epsilon_n<g/2 the local perturbation theorem gives angle<=2 epsilon_n/g and a unique sample top line; this event has probability tending to one. Boundedness in probability at root-n scale yields convergence of the sign-free angle to zero.
For I_2 the top kernel is R^2, so every unit line is leading. For diag(2,1) the top kernel is span(e_1), but e_1 and -e_1 are both unit eigenvectors on that line.

On the explicit four-point law, E(U)=E(V)=E(UV)=0 and E(U^2)=E(V^2)=1. This gives Sigma=[[9,3],[3,4]], D=diag(3,2), and R=[[1,1/2],[1/2,1]]. R has top line span(1,1); Sigma has distinct eigenvalues (13±sqrt(61))/2 and maps (1,1) to (12,7), so its leading line differs.

A_delta=diag(1+delta,1) has gap delta and E_delta=[[0,delta/4],[delta/4,0]] has norm delta/4. The perturbed top eigenvalue is 1+delta/2+sqrt(5)delta/4 and its eigenvector slope is sqrt(5)-2, so the angle is fixed while delta tends to zero.
